resources.title: Old and new objects
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 14 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a forty-minute comparison lesson for three to four pupils. Use generic pictures of a kettle, a telephone and a school bag in older and more recent designs. Pupils choose one pair, find one shared use or visible feature and one paired difference, then keep their own comparison in a book.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!B41/C41: Compare old and new objects (then & now). Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

Week 2 is formative. The owner sets Week 6 as assessing. Success is a matched pair, one accurate similarity and one difference linked to both pictures or their supplied context. The minimum finish uses one pair. A second pair is an extension.

Set Source Cards pages 1–2, Support Cards page 1, the word mat and visible model at each place. Supply books, blank slips and usual aids. Adult may cut the six pictures apart along the white gaps, retaining top/bottom and object-type labels on the reverse, or pupils may point to the whole sheet. Keep the full labelled key available.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and a visible model. Level 2 is the requested scaffold provision, not a qualification level. Supported, Independent and Aspire retain all supports. Exact scribing is available throughout. Read short labels privately on request. No public questioning, cold calling or required reading aloud.

Top row is then, an older design; bottom row is now, a more recent design. These are supplied teaching labels. Both styles may still be used today. The illustrations are invented generic designs, not photographs of dated original objects. No maker, brand, place or community is identified. Shape, position and labels carry meaning without colour.
Thursday 14 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes match an object pair. Keep picture key, bank, stem and matching model on view.
5 minutes source teaching with a short reset; 5 minutes worked bag comparison and quiet hinge; 5 minutes guided kettle or phone comparison.
10 minutes book comparison with a brief reset; 3 minutes private check and response; 2 minutes exit and evidence capture.

“These are two designs of the same kind of thing. Both bags carry things. This bag has buckles. This bag has a zip. I compare the fastening on both.” Point to the pictures. “Use both pictures. You can point or ask me to write.”

Offer buckle/zip and buckle/screen: “Show the pair that compares the same feature.” Buckle/zip is correct for the bags. If unsure, trace the two closures and rebuild one shared category. Parallel check: compare the two kettle handles, top and side. Keep the model visible; do not remove support to test memory.

The pack works entirely with pictures. No heating, boiling, plugs, live calls or personal devices are needed. If the owner adds replicas, use clean, safe, cool, disconnected items under adult direction. Touch is optional. Offer HELP/PASS, a quiet request, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause. No reason is needed in front of the group.

The pupil selects the pair, words or labels and the comparison. The adult writes exact words, reads back quietly and invites keep/change. Record actual prompts and any adult-supplied ideas. Pointing to both relevant features is valid evidence of a selected comparison; copying the model alone is not sufficient.
Thursday 14 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: match one pair, select a shared-use label, point to a paired difference and direct a scribe. Independent: record one similarity and one paired difference in a book. Aspire: compare another pair or ask a question the pictures cannot answer, using the extra stem and model. Every route retains the word bank, starters and model.

Cognition: one step and a small choice set. Communication: quiet wait time, exact scribe and usual aid; plan in any language. SEMH: predictable steps, private help and no personal home questions. Sensory/physical: large picture cards, adult cutting and usual access tools. Use words, shape, position and borders without reliance on colour.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W02-E1: selected pair, one shared use or feature, one paired difference, picture clues and actual help. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil; absent pupils stay blank. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode precede R. E follows actual banking. No actual result is pre-filled.

A repair helper looks closely at an object’s parts before explaining what has changed. Offer authentic pupil words or choices to the Communication portfolio. Do not infer independent reading, writing or award completion from a supported comparison.

resources.title: Staff answers and support
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 14 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Compare old and new objects (then & now). From BUILD Weekly - Spring!B41/C41. Thursday 14 January 2027, P3. Theme: Resilience & Change. This is formative. Week 6 is assessing under the owner brief.

Top row gives older designs; bottom row gives more recent designs. Left: kettles. Middle: telephones. Right: school bags. Any vertical object pair is a valid starter match. These are generic invented illustrations, not documented historical artefacts.

Kettles: both heat water and have a handle, lid and spout; the top-row handle sits above the body, while the bottom-row handle sits at the side. Phones: both allow talk with someone; one has a round dial and handset, the other has a flat screen. School bags: both carry things; one closes with a flap and buckles, the other has a zip. Accept any accurate shared feature and matched-feature difference supported by the two pictures or supplied context.

Uses and older/more recent labels are given context. Pupils can see features, but cannot establish exact age, material composition, weight, price, safety or working condition from a picture. Do not claim a particular manufacturing date or maker. Both design styles may still be in use.

Old does not mean broken or bad; new does not mean best. Colour alone does not date an object. A kettle and a bag are not the matching pair for this task. Comparing a buckle with a screen mixes categories: return to the two bag closures. If a pupil names only one object, prompt for the second picture and a paired feature.
Thursday 14 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Use the fourth pupil-number field only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Check one similarity and one paired difference for each pupil. A shared discussion does not establish each learner’s response.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Scribe exact words or selected labels. Read back privately for keep/change, retaining who selected the ideas and actual prompts. No public questioning or required reading aloud. Use usual aids and quiet wait time.

A second comparison can use the kettle handles. The visible model is “Both kettles heat water. Then has a top handle. Now has a side handle.” An unanswered question can be “How heavy is it?” Do not invent a weight. A thoughtful question is not evidence that its answer is known.

Use HUM-BUILD-S1-W02-E1. Offer authentic words or choices to the Communication portfolio. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s own response precede R. Actual banking precedes E. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks remain separate; no qualification completion is inferred.

slides.notes:
HUM-BUILD-S1-W02 · Year A · Thursday 14 January 2027 · P3
A fair comparison: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Model the school-bag pair using the editable table. Both carry things. The then bag has buckles; the now bag has a zip. This compares fastening with fastening. Quiet hinge: buckle/zip or buckle/screen is a matched-feature pair? Buckle/zip. If unsure, point to each bag closure and rematch. Parallel check: compare kettle handle with kettle handle. Keep bank, stems and model visible.
Outcome verbatim: Compare old and new objects (then & now).

My object pair: 5 minutes.

Words: both, handle, dial, screen. Stems: Both __. Then __. Now __. Model: Both kettles heat water. Then has a top handle. Now has a side handle. Adult reads if wanted.
Outcome verbatim: Compare old and new objects (then & now).

HUM-BUILD-S1-W02 · Year A · Thursday 14 January 2027 · P3
My book record: 10 minutes.
Teacher: At minute 25, include a short reset inside this ten-minute block. Each pupil chooses one pair and records one shared use or visible feature and one paired difference in their book. Supported: point, choose labels and direct an exact scribe. Independent: record using all scaffolds. Aspire: add a second pair with the same stem and model, or a question the pictures do not answer. Never require personal home details.
Outcome verbatim: Compare old and new objects (then & now).

Teacher: Private review. Ask the pupil to show which two pictures support the response. Adult reads exact scribed words back for keep/change. Record actual help. Give one actual audience reply and one NS, then retain the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode before R. No public performance.

shape_text.name: cold-call-detail
shape_text.text:
No public questions or required reading aloud.
Point, private prompt, rephrase, choice.
No live appliances, calls or personal home details.
R: reply, NS, own response. E: actual banking.

slides.notes:
HUM-BUILD-S1-W02 · Year A · Thursday 14 January 2027 · P3
Adult support brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Hidden adult brief: Level 2 means word bank, sentence starter and visible model on every task, not a qualification level. Prompt ladder: point, short private prompt, rephrase, choice/scaffold, model the first step then return the task. Use generic picture cards. No heat, plugs, calls, live devices or personal disclosures. Supplied design labels are not proof of an individual object’s age. Actual reply, NS and own response precede R; actual banking precedes E.
Outcome verbatim: Compare old and new objects (then & now).
